propositions: Juju storage is a data volume
it is provided by a cloud
correction: Juju storage is a block device or filesystem made available to a charm by a storage provider, which can be a cloud service (ebs) or the machine itself (loop, rootfs, tmpfs).
note: Generic providers are not cloud-provided.

propositions: <size> is the size of each volume
correction: <size> is the minimum size of each storage instance (in MiB internally; accepts M,G,T,P,E,Z,Y with optional iB/B suffix).

propositions: Default pool when none is given is the default storage pool
correction: The default pool is the model's default for the charm's storage kind (the storage-default-block-source / storage-default-filesystem-source setting, else the provider's recommended pool such as ebs on EC2, rootfs for generic filesystem, loop for generic block).
note: Depends on kind and provider.

propositions: Default count is the charm minimum, or 1 if optional
correction: With no directive the count defaults to the charm's count-min (0 when optional); when a directive is given without a count, the CLI parser sets 1.
note: ParseDirective sets Count=1 (directive.go:95) and it is sent as an override, replacing count-min.

propositions: With no directive, storage goes on rootfs
correction: With no directive the model's default pool for the storage kind is used: rootfs for filesystem and loop for block on generic IaaS, ebs on EC2, and so on.

propositions: Pool creation requires name, provider type, attributes as key=value pairs
Example attributes are tags, size, path
correction: Pool creation takes <name> <provider> [<key>=<value> ...]; valid attributes are provider-specific (for example volume-type, iops, encrypted for ebs) and 'name' and 'type' are reserved.
note: tags, size, path are not attributes of the common providers.

propositions: loop, rootfs and tmpfs are available on all clouds
correction: loop, rootfs and tmpfs are available on all machine (IaaS) clouds; Kubernetes models offer kubernetes, rootfs and tmpfs, and reject loop.
note: loop ValidateForK8s returns NotValid (loop.go:~45).

propositions: The user's key must be in the model
The user needs admin on the model
correction: The key must be in the model and the user needs model admin access or controller superuser access.
note: Superuser also qualifies (permission.go:175; sshclient/facade.go:93).

propositions: For bare metal/VM, a constraint is a minimum
For system containers/k8s containers it is a maximum
correction: Constraints are minimums when selecting machines or instance types (cores, mem, root-disk), and become limits for LXD containers (limits.cpu, limits.memory) and for Kubernetes pods, where Juju sets both requests and limits.
note: core/constraints/constraints.go:61-72 says 'at least'. internal/provider/kubernetes/application/constraints.go:335-340 sets both Requests and Limits, so k8s is not only a maximum. LXD VMs also get limits.

propositions: allocate-public-ip takes true/false
It decides whether machines get an IP reachable outside the cloud network
It applies to GCE, EC2, Azure and OpenStack
correction: It is honoured by GCE, Azure, OCI, OpenStack and EC2 (EC2 only acts on false, and its validator lists the constraint as unsupported so a warning is issued); it is unsupported on MAAS, LXD, vSphere, Kubernetes and unmanaged.
note: ec2/environ.go:270 lists AllocatePublicIP in unsupportedConstraints yet ec2/environ.go:752-756 uses it. OCI also supports it, so the provider list omits OCI.

propositions: Public cloud instances get a public IP by default
correction: GCE, Azure and OCI default to allocating a public IP; OpenStack allocates a floating IP only when the constraint is true; EC2 follows the subnet's setting.
note: core/constraints/constraints.go:115-118: nil or true means allocate. openstack/provider.go:1383-1386 withPublicIP defaults to false.

propositions: arch valid values are amd64, arm64, ppc64el, s390x, riscv64
correction: Juju recognises those five architectures, but each provider restricts the vocabulary (EC2, Azure, OCI: amd64 and arm64; vSphere: amd64; LXD and MAAS: whatever the server reports).
note: Provider vocabularies in ec2/environ.go:277, azure/environ.go:471, vsphere/environ_policy.go:96, oci/environ.go:331.

propositions: cpu-power is an integer
100 units equals roughly a 2007-era Xeon, as reflected by 1 Amazon vCPU
correction: cpu-power is an integer where 100 is equivalent to 1 Amazon ECU, roughly a single 2007-era Xeon.
note: Code comment says ECU, not vCPU. EC2 defaults cpu-power to 100 (ec2/image.go:78).

propositions: With juju deploy, image-id must be used with --base
--base specifies the OS of the image
correction: When image-id is used, a base must be given explicitly, either with --base or as an explicitly configured default-base; for bundles an explicit base or default base is required.
note: Error: 'base must be explicitly provided when image-id constraint is used'. Check applies to model constraints too (deployer.go:315, bundle.go:160-168).

propositions: Currently only AWS (instance profiles) and Azure (managed identities, from 3.6) support it
correction: AWS (instance profiles), Azure (managed identities) and GCE (service accounts) support instance-role.
note: gce/environ_broker.go:188-189 uses the constraint as the service account. The 3.6 start date is unverifiable here.

propositions: ip-family values: ipv4, ipv6, dual
ipv6-only is not supported by any provider
Details per cloud
correction: The parser accepts ipv4, ipv6 and dual, but only Azure honours the constraint (ipv4 and dual); every other provider lists it as unsupported and ignores it with a warning.
note: Azure vocabulary excludes ipv6 so the ipv6-only statement holds. core/network/ipfamily/ipfamily.go.

propositions: Optional M/G/T/P suffix means mega/giga/tera/peta bytes
correction: Suffixes M, G, T, P multiply by powers of 1024 (G = 1024 M), so they denote binary units (MiB, GiB, TiB, PiB); no suffix means MiB.
note: mbSuffixes map. Float values are accepted and rounded up (parseSize:868).

propositions: Spaces can be positive or negative with ^ prefix
The example is valid and means in storage and db but not logging/public
Only EC2 and MAAS support spaces
correction: Space constraints are resolved for any provider whose SupportsSpaces is true (EC2, MAAS, Azure, GCE, OpenStack, LXD, unmanaged); Kubernetes and OCI do not support spaces.
note: Syntax and ^ prefix hold (constraints.go:207-250). Azure, OpenStack and LXD consume SubnetsToZones/SpaceSubnets (azure/environ_network.go:429, openstack/provider.go:1485, lxd/environ_broker.go).

propositions: tags is a comma-delimited list of tags on the machine
correction: tags are comma-delimited labels honoured by MAAS (machine tags) and Kubernetes (affinity labels, key=value form); other providers do not support them.
note: core/constraints/constraints.go:764.

propositions: Tags can be negative with ^
Example tags=virtual,^dualnic is valid
Supported by MAAS and Kubernetes for pod affinity
correction: MAAS honours ^ negation; on Kubernetes tags must be key=value pairs (optionally prefixed pod., anti-pod. or node.) and become node, pod affinity or anti-affinity, so the example tags=virtual,^dualnic is a MAAS form only.
note: kubernetes/application/constraints.go:75-84 rejects entries without exactly one '='.

propositions: virt-type is the virtualisation type
Only LXD and OpenStack support it
correction: virt-type is accepted by LXD (container, virtual-machine), OpenStack (kvm, lxd) and MAAS (virtual-machine); EC2, GCE, Azure, vSphere, OCI and Kubernetes list it as unsupported.
note: MAAS registers a VirtType vocabulary and does not list it unsupported.

propositions: A binding restricts the endpoint's traffic to the space's subnets
correction: A binding selects which space's addresses an endpoint uses (network-get / relation data) and which subnets a machine is placed in; Juju does not enforce traffic restrictions.
note: GetUnitEndpointNetworkInfo returns endpoint addresses by bound space.

propositions: A user is a person who can log in to a controller
correction: A Juju user is an identity (local, or external such as everyone@external) that can authenticate to a controller; it need not be a person.
note: Users table also holds external users and service-style users like juju-metrics.

propositions: Login uses username and password
correction: Users log in with a username and password, or with macaroon/external identity or JWT-based credentials.

propositions: Bootstrap creates user named admin
Admin is prompted to create a password when first attempting to log out
correction: The bootstrap user is named admin and gets a random password stored in the client; logout fails with a 'preventing account loss' error until the password is changed with juju change-user-password (or --force is used), without any prompt.

propositions: Every user has an access level
correction: Every user normally holds a controller access level (login or superuser) but access can be NoAccess after revoke.

propositions: add-user default is controller login
Login level allows only register and login
correction: A user added with add-user has controller login access; this lets them log in and do things permitted without extra grants (e.g. change own password, see models/offers they are granted), but nothing on models until granted.

propositions: Superuser is granted automatically at bootstrap
Username admin confers it
correction: Bootstrap grants superuser to the bootstrap user (named admin); the username admin itself has no special effect, and other users get superuser via juju grant.

propositions: Cloud add-model access lets a user grant model-level permissions
correction: Cloud add-model access lets a user add models on that cloud; model permissions are granted with juju grant by a model admin or superuser.

propositions: CLI blocks and waits by default
correction: juju run blocks by default for up to 60 seconds (juju exec 5 minutes), unless --background or --wait is given.

propositions: Synchronous behaviour suits pipelines
correction: Waiting is bounded by the default timeout, so long actions return before completion in pipelines unless --wait is set.

propositions: Progress messages are shown on the terminal
correction: Progress messages are streamed only when a single task is running.

propositions: Generic env vars plus action-specific ones
Two action-specific variables listed
correction: Action-specific variables are JUJU_ACTION_NAME, JUJU_ACTION_UUID and JUJU_ACTION_TAG.

propositions: Application lives in one model
Application consists of one or more units
correction: An application lives in one model and may have zero or more units (scale can be 0).
note: Applications can be scaled to zero units; not exhaustively confirmed in code.

propositions: A unit is a deployed charm
correction: A unit is one instance of an application's charm, running on a machine or in a pod.

propositions: Units occupy machines
correction: Units run on machines on machine clouds and in pods on Kubernetes.

propositions: Unit name is <application>/<number>
The leader keyword is a unit ID in the name
correction: A unit name is <application>/<number>; the <application>/leader form is accepted only as a command-line target, not as the unit's name.
note: Name regexp allows only numbers; leader appears in ssh/run help (cmd/juju/ssh/ssh.go:40, cmd/juju/action/run.go:69).

propositions: mysql/0 is valid
mysql/leader is a unit name
correction: mysql/0 is a unit name; mysql/leader is a command-line target alias.

propositions: Leader is authoritative source for application status and configuration
correction: The leader holds the application-level lease and may set application status and application relation data; user config is shared by all units.
note: Not directly confirmed in what was searched; contradicts unit:9 claim that config is shared.

propositions: Units share charm, relations, config
Leader manages the application lifecycle
correction: All units share charm, relations and config; the leader may write application-level data and charms typically use it for coordination, but Juju does not give it lifecycle management.

propositions: Consume validates permission and creates a local proxy application, then integrates
correction: Consuming creates a local remote-application proxy after a permission check, and integrate is a separate relation step.
note: Proxy creation confirmed; the permission check wasn't traced fully.
